Information Criterion Calculations via Julia

Source: R/penalty_selection.R
information_criteria.Rd

Compute information criteria using efficient 'Julia' backends via the 'JuliaCall' package. These functions are useful for variable selection and model comparison in high-dimensional settings. Each function returns either the computed criterion value, or a list with additional data.

Usage

Calculate_AIC(Y, X)

Calculate_AICc(Y, X)

Calculate_AttIC(Y, X)

Calculate_SIC(Y, X)

Calculate_BIC(Y, X)

Calculate_CAIC(Y, X)

Calculate_CAICF(Y, X)

Calculate_EBIC(Y, X, P = ncol(X))

Calculate_GIC2(Y, X, P = ncol(X))

Calculate_GIC3(Y, X, P = ncol(X))

Calculate_GIC4(Y, X, P = ncol(X))

Calculate_GIC5(Y, X, P = ncol(X))

Calculate_GIC6(Y, X, P = ncol(X))

Arguments

Y

A numeric response: a vector of length n, or an n x q matrix for a multivariate response (CAICF supports vector responses only).

X

A numeric design matrix (n × p).

P

(only for EBIC and GIC2–GIC6) integer total number of candidate predictors. Defaults to ncol(X).

Value

A named list with components:

CriterionValue

Numeric scalar of the selected information criterion.

InverseMatrix

Matrix inverse used in computation (if applicable).

Details

Every criterion has the form \(Y^\top H Y / n - p(n, K)\), where \(H\) is the hat matrix of the \(K\) selected columns and \(p(n, K)\) is the penalty (Xiao and Walker, 2026). With \(\hat\sigma^2 = \mathrm{RSS}/(n - K)\) and \(P\) the number of candidate predictors, the supported criteria are:

  • AIC, Akaike information criterion (Akaike, 1974): \(2K\hat\sigma^2/n\).

  • AICc, AIC corrected for small samples (Hurvich and Tsai, 1989): \((K+1)\hat\sigma^2/(n-K-2)\).

  • BIC, Bayesian information criterion (Schwarz, 1978): \(K\hat\sigma^2\log(n)/n\).

  • CAIC, consistent AIC (Bozdogan, 1987): \(K\hat\sigma^2(\log n + 1)/n\).

  • CAICF, consistent AIC with Fisher information (Bozdogan, 1987): the CAIC penalty plus \(\hat\sigma^2 \log\det(X^\top X/\hat\sigma^2)/n\).

  • SIC, square-root information criterion (Shao, 1997; Xiao and Walker, 2026): \(K\hat\sigma^2/\sqrt{n}\).

  • GIC2–GIC6, generalized information criteria for high dimensions (Kim, Kwon and Choi, 2012), with penalties \(K\hat\sigma^2 P^{1/3}/n\), \(2K\hat\sigma^2\log(P)/n\), \(2K\hat\sigma^2(\log P + \log\log P)/n\), \(K\hat\sigma^2\log\log(n)\log(P)/n\) and \(K\hat\sigma^2\log(n)\log(P)/n\).

  • EBIC, extended BIC (Chen and Chen, 2008): \(K\hat\sigma^2\{\log n + \gamma\log\binom{P}{K}\}/n\), with \(\gamma = 0.6\) by default.

  • AttIC, an attention-weighted criterion specific to this package: the fit term is replaced by \(Y^\top \mathrm{softmax}(HY)\) and the penalty is that of SIC.

References

Akaike, H. (1974). A new look at the statistical model identification. IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control, 19(6), 716–723. doi:10.1109/TAC.1974.1100705

Bozdogan, H. (1987). Model selection and Akaike's information criterion (AIC): The general theory and its analytical extensions. Psychometrika, 52(3), 345–370. doi:10.1007/BF02294361

Chen, J. and Chen, Z. (2008). Extended Bayesian information criteria for model selection with large model spaces. Biometrika, 95(3), 759–771. doi:10.1093/biomet/asn034

Hurvich, C. M. and Tsai, C.-L. (1989). Regression and time series model selection in small samples. Biometrika, 76(2), 297–307. doi:10.1093/biomet/76.2.297

Kim, Y., Kwon, S. and Choi, H. (2012). Consistent model selection criteria on high dimensions. Journal of Machine Learning Research, 13, 1037–1057. https://jmlr.org/papers/v13/kim12a.html

Schwarz, G. (1978). Estimating the dimension of a model. The Annals of Statistics, 6(2), 461–464. doi:10.1214/aos/1176344136

Shao, J. (1997). An asymptotic theory for linear model selection. Statistica Sinica, 7(2), 221–264. https://www3.stat.sinica.edu.tw/statistica/j7n2/j7n21/j7n21.htm

Xiao, Y. and Walker, S. (2026). Fast variable selection under \(\ell_0\) regularization in high-dimensions. Statistics and Computing, 36(3), 100. doi:10.1007/s11222-026-10853-5

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
if (interactive() && requireNamespace("JuliaCall", quietly = TRUE)) {
  setup_julia(install_julia = FALSE)
  X <- matrix(rnorm(100), ncol = 5)
  Y <- rnorm(20)
  out1 <- Calculate_AIC(Y, X)
  out2 <- Calculate_EBIC(Y, X)        # uses P = ncol(X) by default
}
} # }
